subject: Supply-chain dependencies & evidence for EU procurement review
messages:
From: Anika Sørensen <anika.sorensen@euromed-health.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@euromed-health.com
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 09:15:00 +0100
Subject: Request: supply chain dependency matrix & EU dataflow for Redwood Inference

Hi Vanessa,

We are completing the vendor intake for Redwood as part of our EU procurement packet. Two asks to support our security review:

1) A detailed subprocessor/dependency matrix that lists any third parties with access to customer data (purpose, region, whether they process plaintext, contractual protections).
2) A high-level dataflow diagram specific to EU-customer workflows (ingest -> processing -> storage), and any retention/replication behavior.

Can you also point us to your most recent SOC 2 report (redacted if needed) and confirm which KMS providers you support for EU deployments? We need to finalize by EOD Wednesday (2027-04-14) to stay on track.

Thanks — if easier, a single zip or a Drive folder link is fine.

Best,
Anika Sørensen
Procurement Manager
Euromed Health

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Anika Sørensen <anika.sorensen@euromed-health.com>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, mina_haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 11:02:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Request: supply chain dependency matrix & EU dataflow for Redwood Inference

Hi Anika — thanks for the clear list. We can provide both items. Quick clarifying points so we scope correctly:

- Do you want the matrix filtered to only subprocessors that can handle EU-region data, or all global subprocessors with a column indicating region?
- For KMS: do you need customer-managed KMS details (e.g., supported BYOK providers) or just which managed KMS we integrate with?

Plan: Marcus will attach an initial CSV (subprocessor matrix) and a PNG dataflow. Mina will attach the SOC 2 report redacted for customer delivery. I will include a short cover note and links to the shared Drive where we keep evidence. Expect the first package in the next business day.

If there are tight constraints on timelines or you need deeper evidence (e.g., access logs, on-demand audit), flag that now so we can surface to security.

Cheers,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Enterprise Sales (EMEA)
Redwood Inference

From: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Anika Sørensen <anika.sorensen@euromed-health.com>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: mina_haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 08:40:00 +0100
Subject: Fwd: initial package: subprocessor matrix + EU dataflow

Attachments: redwood_subprocessor_matrix_v1.csv (CSV), redwood_eu_dataflow_diagram.png (image), SOC2-Report-Redwood-2026.pdf (PDF - redacted)

Anika / team — attaching the files Vanessa mentioned. Summary highlights from the matrix:

- We list 18 subprocessors total; 6 are EU-region (data centers or regional analytics providers). Column breakdown includes: subprocessor name, service type, data types accessed (tokenized/plaintext/metadata), processing purpose, contract status (standard DPA / custom), and region.
- Access to plaintext customer data: only our core storage provider for EU deployments and one analytics vendor (both under strict contractual NDA and scoped access).
- Encryption: customer data at rest is AES-256; in transit is TLS1.3. For Redwood Private/VPC deployments customers can opt for customer-managed keys (BYOK) via Azure Key Vault or AWS KMS (both available in EU regions).
- Retention/replication: primary EU storage is limited to EU region. Backup replication to cross-region is configurable and marked in the matrix per-customer.

SOC 2: redacted copy attached. For full (non-redacted) report we require an NDA/TA.

If you want, we can produce a short one-page mapping: "Which subprocessor handles X" for the legal team.

--Marcus
Senior Information Security Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Anika Sørensen <anika.sorensen@euromed-health.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:11:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Fwd: initial package: subprocessor matrix + EU dataflow

Vanessa / Marcus — thanks, this is helpful and arrives ahead of schedule. A couple of follow-ups to close our internal checklist:

- Can you confirm which of the listed EU subprocessors have the technical ability to decrypt customer data (i.e., have plaintext access) versus only processing tokenized/encrypted material? Please call out names.
- Our legal team needs SLA language confirming a 99.9% availability target for production inference endpoints for Dedicated/EU incidents — do you have a standard clause or reference to include?

If you can send a short reply (or an annotated matrix) by EOD today, that would keep us on track for procurement sign-off on Wednesday.

Regards,
Anika

On Sun, Apr 11, 2027 at 08:40 vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Attached the initial package.

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Anika Sørensen <anika.sorensen@euromed-health.com>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, mina_haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 16:23:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Fwd: initial package: subprocessor matrix + EU dataflow

Hi Anika — quick answers inline and attached an annotated CSV (redwood_subprocessor_matrix_v1-annotated.csv) with the plaintext-access column you requested. High-level:

- EU subprocessors with plaintext access: 2 (EUCoreStorage Ltd. — host for EU dedicated storage; and EU-Analytics S.A. — analytics only under restricted service accounts). All other subprocessors only receive pseudonymized or encrypted datasets.
- SLA: For Redwood Dedicated in EU we offer a 99.9% monthly availability commitment in our standard Dedicated Services Addendum. I attached a PDF excerpt with the exact SLA wording and remedies (see attachment SOC2-Report-Redwood-2026.pdf includes the addendum excerpt). If you need contract language (redlines), I can loop legal.

Next steps we propose:
- I will drop the annotated matrix and dataflow diagram into the Drive link: https://drive.google.com/redwood/euprocurement/PR-4321 (already uploaded).
- If your legal team needs the full non-redacted SOC 2 or raw access logs for audit, please send an NDA request and we will coordinate with Security for a controlled view.

If anything is missing for sign-off tomorrow, call me directly at +44 20 7123 4500.

Best regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Enterprise Sales (EMEA)
Redwood Inference
